name: Taurodontia-absent teeth-sparse hair syndrome
aliases: Taurodontism with hypodontia and hypotrichosis syndrome
Taurodontia with dental agenesis and sparse hair syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Taurodontia-absent teeth-sparse hair syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of taurodontism characterized by enlarged pulp chambers and apically displaced furcation of molar teeth
Congenital absence of multiple permanent teeth (hypodontia or oligodontia)
Sparse, thin scalp hair (hypotrichosis) evident from infancy or early childhood
Mild facial dysmorphism including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: taurodontism, congenital absence of multiple teeth, and sparse scalp hair
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and radiographic; genetic testing may support but is not routinely available.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enlarged pulp chambers with apical displacement of furcation
Multiple permanent teeth absent from eruption
Sparse, thin hair apparent from infancy

common.notes: Prominent forehead noted in early childhood
Underdeveloped midfacial region contributing to facial dysmorphism
Permanent teeth eruption delayed beyond normal age
searchTerms: late coming in of adult teeth

common.notes: Sparse eyebrow hair often accompanies scalp hypotrichosis

occasional.notes: Defective enamel formation leading to enamel pits or thin enamel

searchTerms: one side of face slightly different

occasional.notes: Mild xerosis noted in some patients

rare.notes: Reduced ability to sweat reported in rare cases
Occasional mild hearing impairment due to middle ear anomalies
Increased risk of tooth decay secondary to enamel defects

imaging: Panoramic dental radiographs showing taurodontism with enlarged pulp chambers
Radiographic evidence of multiple missing permanent teeth
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
other: Clinical examination revealing sparse scalp hair and dental anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: More widespread ectodermal involvement including nails and skin
Often associated with hypohidrosis and dental anomalies but different hair pattern
Severe hypohidrosis leading to heat intolerance
Characteristic facial features including saddle nose and thick lips
Genetic testing positive for EDA gene mutations

redFlags: Severe dental agenesis impairing mastication and nutrition
Signs of associated systemic involvement such as hearing loss or skin infections
specialistType: Dentist specialized in pediatric or developmental dental anomalies
references: Pindborg JJ. Taurodontism. Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol. 1970;29(5):688-700.
Wright JT, et al. Dental anomalies in ectodermal dysplasias. Am J Med Genet A. 2015;167A(1):1-9.
